chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The spirit of faith is taken from him as long as he is upon her belly; so when he descends, faith returns.
I said to him, 'What is your view if he only considers it?' He said, 'No.'
Do you see that if he considers stealing, would his hand be cut?
ai.seo_question: Does the act of urinating nullify faith according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the distinction between the spiritual state of 'faith' (Iman) and legal culpability (Taklif), noting that the 'spirit of faith' is temporarily veiled during urination but returns upon standing. He further clarifies that mere internal consideration (hamm) does not trigger physical penalties, using the example of theft where the hand is only cut upon actual execution, not mere thought. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly principle that minor ritual impurities or internal states do not nullify the core of faith, while legal punishments require concrete action.
